newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MOYA TO SPEARHEAD VALENCIA ATTACK AGAINST BAYERN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOYA TO SPEARHEAD VALENCIA ATTACK AGAINST BAYERN MUNICH.

text.p: Former Seville striker Gabriel Moya will spearhead the Valencia attack against Bayern Munich in their UEFA Cup first round second leg tie on Tuesday in the absence of Brazilian Romario.
Valencia take a handsome 3-0 lead into the match at Munich's Olympic stadium against last year's champions.
Romario scored Valencia's second goal in the 2-1 win over Tenerife on Saturday but injured his knee.

Striker Jose Galvez will also be absent through injury while the Spaniards' defence has been hit by injuries to key players with neither captain Francisco Camarasa not Jorge Otero expected to fly to Germany.
Valencia's victory on Saturday against another of the Spanish sides involved in the UEFA Cup was their first of the season.
Bayern went top of the Bundesliga standings by beating Karlsruhe 1-0 on Saturday and remain unbeaten in the league this season.
But club president Franz Beckenbauer is clearly concerned with their present form, with just 14 goals in seven games.

"If we want to advance we are going to have to play two or three levels better," Beckenbauer wrote in his weekly newspaper column. "The team are going to have to shift a few gears higher if they want to prove to Valencia that they are among the best in Europe."
Striker Juergen Klinsmann continues to struggle and has been replaced in four matches this season, although he played the full 90 minutes against Karlsruhe.
While Valencia are handily placed to overturn Bayern, Tenerife have a battle on their hands against Maccabi after letting the Israelis back into the first round tie.
Tenerife won 3-2 after taking a 2-0 lead and have lost both their subsequent league games.
Espanyol, held 2-2 in Nicosia by Apoel Cyprus, may be without French forward Nicolas Quedec who pulled a muscle in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Athletic Bilbao.
Each of the Italian sides -- Internazionale, Parma and Roma -- take first leg leads into Tuesday's matches.
Inter, with a 3-0 lead over French side Giungamp, look to have the easiest task.

Once again, their English coach Roy Hodgson has an embarrassment of international talent from which to choose, with Frenchmen Joceyln Angloma and Yuori Djorkaeff, Swiss Ciriaco Sforza, England's Paul Ince, Dutchman Aron Winter, Argentine Javier Zanetti and Chilean Ivan Zamorano all likely to play.
"I can't say we're really into the Milan match. We're thinking much more about our league match against Paris St Germain next Sunday", said Giungamp coach Francis Smerecki.
Lazio, who held Inter to a 1-1 home draw on Saturday, take only a one-goal lead into their home UEFA tie with another French side, Lens.

The Italians will be without suspended defender Giuseppe Favalli but field a strong side including Italian internationals Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi in attack, with Czech Pavel Nedved and Italo-Australian Paul Okon in midfield.
Lens are without injured defenders Jean-Guy Wallemme, Cyril Magnier and Frederic Dehu and have not scored a goal in their last four matches.
Roma, disappointing in a 4-1 home defeat by Sampdoria on Saturday, take a three-goal lead to Russia for their tie with Dynamo Moscow.
With strikers Francesco Totti and Marco Delvecchio injured and Uruguyan Daniel Fonseca due for a rest, Roma may start with just one striker, Argentine Abel Balbo.
Parma, 3-2 league winners against Reggiana on Saturday, rely on their $15 million dollar signing Enrico Chiesa along with Gianfranco Zola for their away tie against Portuguese side Vitoria Guimaraes.
Parma take a 2-1 lead into the tie and their line-up should also include Argentine Nestor Sensini in defence with Frenchman Daniel Bravo alongside Dino Baggio and Massimo Crippa in midfield.
Monaco, who play on Wednesday, are the only French side optimistic about their chances of progressing further at the expense of Polish side Hutnik Krakow
The team from the principality, 1-0 winners in the first leg, will take the field without French international Eric Di Meco and Dane Dan Petersen.
